lines.en: I knock on Futaba’s door and wait for her to answer...
But she never does.
And I go home without accomplishing anything.
A few hours later, on the other side of town...
And roughly one hundred feet underneath the surface...
: And so concludes another successful adventure! This time, without anyone being forced out of their comfort zone or...
: Or up against the door of a crowded train.
: You’ve been playing “those games” again, haven’t you?
: Aye! But that has naught to do with my anecdote and everything to do with why I must still rely on those games! But I digress!
: Well...I’m glad you had fun, Molly. It was certainly a...productive trip, if not anything else.
: Did you wind up getting everything you need for your costume? Because I’m hoping to start work on them Monday and I’m...actually not even sure if I know what you’ll be going as this year.
: Yeah...that’s kind of the problem. I’m not really sure what to do this time around. So while you and Yasu were fabric-shopping, I was...
: I was...buying...other things...
: You went into that section without me?! How could you?! And...how did you?! They always stop me whenever I try!
: If you were shopping for naughty things, God will find out and replace your arms with snakes. He sees all.
: What?! No! I was talking about books!
: Then why would you make it sound like you were doing something so impure?! I know lewd emphasis when I hear it!
: Because I...I was talking about those kinds of books, Molly. The ones Yasu isn’t allowed to read yet.
: Do they contain inappropriate content?
: Hah...yes, Yasu. Yes they do.
: Hmph. I hope you enjoy your snake arms.
: Tch. You should’ve just said that from the start so I didn’t get my hopes up.
: If you need recommendations for a costume, though- I’d be happy to help, Futaba. I started work on a Kafka costume for Tsuneyo but I had to bench the idea because it kept making me feel things.
: I don’t think I...have the energy or confidence needed to pull that character off.
: What are you talking about? You pulled Himeko off just fine and she practically bleeds confidence.
: Yes, but she also has a certain amount of...motherly energy that Kafka lacks. And I don’t want to walk around the Halloween party pretending that I like to...step on people.
: Don’t knock it ‘til you try it, Xessaxia. At the rate you’re consuming those smut novels, you could very well unlock new aspects of your personality that even I would gawk at.
: Shh...we have a child with us, Molly. We can’t exactly talk about the things that “even you would gawk at.”
: Nonsense. Yasu might be a child now, but it’s only a matter of time until she has the same secret folders on her laptop that we do.
: I abstain from using technology as it exposes me to information that has not yet been filtered through Him and opens me up to being falsely guided.
: Also, Touka says I’m not allowed. But I don’t want to anyway.
: Like I said...there is a child present.
: Hah...at this rate, I’ll be bitin’ the feckin’ bullet and just finishin’ the costume for Tsuneyo. Fantasies be damned.
: You’ve gotta figure something out sooner rather than later though, Futaba. The party’s right around the corner at this rate and if I don’t know what you’re after, I might not be able to help.
: It’s fine, Molly. I’m nowhere near your level, but I still know my way around a sewing machine and can always just make my own costume if I really have to.
: Besides, my interests are...elsewhere for the time being.
: How many of those books have you even read so far? I feel like that’s all you ever do now. It’s like you’re not even a real otaku anymore.
: I still keep up with the things we’re reading in club. But, as far as my personal books go, maybe...fifty this year?
: Friggin’ Christ, that many?! I don’t think I’ve read fifty books in my life.
: It’s not as much as it sounds. Just compare that to how much anime you watch.
: I can finish most books in less than a week, so the time commitment isn’t nearly as bad as having to devote three months of my life to another unoriginal harem comedy.
: You leave the bread and butter of the anime industry out of this. Just because you’re becoming a normie doesn’t mean you get to talk down on us now. I won’t allow it.
: Trust me, if you knew what I bought today, you would certainly not be calling me a normie.
: I am suddenly intrigued...
: And I am suddenly being tested again. But my faith knows no bounds, so your evil books will not tempt me.
: Well, let’s put it this way- Nodoka wrote it. And, as I’m sure you know, she’s not exactly the most “wholesome” girl out there.
: Nodoka? Like, Nodoka Nodoka? The Goddess of Impurity herself? I knew she was a writer, but I didn’t realize she was actually published.

: I’m pretty sure she had her first work published when she was around...ten years old, I think? I’ve lost track of how much she’s put out since then. She never tells me about any of her new releases, though.

: I think she’s, like...trying to “preserve my innocence” or something. But, at this point, all innocence I once had is gone and I am now an all-encompassing ball of impurity that rivals even the Goddess herself.
: There is but one God and He is unrivaled. This is heresy of the highest degree.
: How...long is this book, exactly?
: I’m not sure. Normal novel length, I guess? I don’t really know anything about it. But I’ll let you borrow it once I’m done if you want.
: She’s an extremely talented writer, but I don’t think I’ve ever actually finished anything she’s done before as her...raciness was a little too much for me before I got into romance novels.
: I think I’m ready now but, then again, this is Nodoka we’re talking about- so it’s equally possible that I’m going to put it down within minutes and be overcome by the urge to take a shower.
: If this pseudo-normie book of hers is anything even remotely close to that last thing you said, I would very much like to borrow it.
: And I would very much like to burn it as it sounds like something that should not exist.
: It’s just a book, Yasu. And even if you disagree with what’s inside of it, burning it won’t do anything. We should be preserving literature of all types, not destroying it.
: A terrible fate will befall you if you read this book. I can hear it in the screeching of the train upon the tracks. And the voice of my God tells me you must stay away.
: Which reagents did you use to cast Divination just now? I need to make sure they’re worth at least 25 gp.
: The air and all the thoughts within it.
: I’ll allow it.
: Yasu, it’s fine. Like I said, it’s just a book. If worse comes to worst and I feel a “terrible fate” creeping up on me, I can just put it down.
: You do not understand! You are making the wrong choice! You’re damning us all!
: N-Nothing to see here, folks! She’s never been on a train before! She doesn’t know how this works!
: Yasu, shh! You can’t do that in here. Yelling is fine, but only if you wait until we get off, okay?
: But you-
: Shh!
: We can talk when we reach our stop...
: Hah...I’m glad that’s over. Yasu’s always a handful, but I wasn’t expecting her to flip out on me like that.
: I guess Molly and I will just have to talk about this in secret if she does wind up borrowing it.
: That’s not important right now, though. It’s finally time to read.
: Ughhhhh...having a job is hard.
: Or not.
: Futabaaaaa...rub my shoulders...
: Welcome home, Rika. I take it you...had an exhausting day?
: Exhausting is putting it lightly. I feel like I’m gonna die.
: And...and what did you have to do exactly? Because I was...under the assumption your only responsibility was...being the advisor for the light music club.
: Yeah but nobody ever told me how much advice they’d need. And what’s even worse is I already forgot where the ropes are.
: And...what did you need ropes for exactly?
: Putting an end to my misery...
: Please don’t.
: You want me to be miserable forever?
: No...I want you to remain alive because I love you and Rin loves you. But, if it’s not too much trouble, I’d really like it if-
: Whatcha got there?
: If I could read in peace for a little while.
: The Light of...Last...hey, wait a minute. I know this book.
: You...you do?
: Yeah, I was at the signing event for it. Were you there too?
: No, I...I just got it today. And I didn’t even realize you read books, Rika.
: I don’t.
: Then...why were you at the signing exactly? And...where even was this signing? I would have liked to have gone.

: Some book store. I don’t really remember. I just saw a line and got into it thinking there’d be something exciting at the end. And I guess I wasn’t wrong since there were a bunch of single women there, but...
: But all that did was awaken further darkness within me...
: I’m sure you’ll...find someone else soon enough. And...hopefully somewhere else to stay.
: What, are you trying to get rid of me too now? I can’t even count on my second daughter to back me up while I’m homeless?
: I didn’t really mean that. You can stay here as long as you like. I was just kind of hoping I’d be able to read in peace tonight since Rin is working late.
: Are you calling me loud and unwanted? Does my presence bother you, Princess Futaba?
: Your presence does not “bother me,” Mistress Rika. I simply require some alone time.
: Are you even old enough to be reading this kind of stuff? Do I need to call your parents and tell them their daughter’s starting her “bad girl” phase?
: You definitely don’t have to do that. In fact...please don’t do that. I’d much prefer that the types of books I’ve been reading lately aren’t really divulged to or...known by anyone.
: Except your best friend’s mom, who now knows you’re up to no good.
: Yes. Except my best friend’s mom, who now knows I’m up to no good.
: Well, I was planning on hitting the hay a little early tonight. But, considering you want your “alone time,” I guess I can see what Wakana and Imani are up to. Maybe Sensei will be there too.
: Are you and him getting along well?
: I...think so? Maybe?...
: I thought we were, but...I’m not really sure how he sees me anymore.
: Did...something happen?
: Nothing you need to be worried about, kiddo. Aunt Rika’s just not the best when it comes to the impressions she gives people sometimes.
: Well, if it means anything, I think you’re great. And I’m sure Sensei will see that too.
: Hope so, kid. Hope so.
: Anyway, I’m out! Enjoy your book. That author girl was weird as shit. And she looks mad similar to your friend with the glasses on the second floor.
: I’m sure that was just a...coincidence...
: Night, Futaba! Don’t stay up too late.
: Goodnight, Rika! Take your time coming home. I’m hoping to get at least the first half of this done tonight, and I have absolutely no clue how long that will take.
: Those other girls seemed to like it a lot, so I’m sure it’ll be a good time even if it’s quick. Like that time I fingered the singer of-
: Okay, Rika! Bye!
: Sorry! Bye! Have fun!
: I’m sure I will.
: I’m sure I will...
One hour later...
